elements.element: Customer may assign to any affiliate without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The clause permits assignment without approval only to a “financially responsible affiliate,” which is narrower than an unrestricted right to assign to any affiliate.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly eliminates approval for an assignment by Client to a successor in a merger.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in an acquisition without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly eliminates approval for an assignment by Client to a successor in an acquisition.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly eliminates approval for an assignment by Client to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: Vendor must obtain Customer consent for every assignment.
elements.evidence: TrueLink may assign to a financially responsible affiliate without Client approval, contrary to the required one-way consent restriction.

elements.element: Customer must not unreasonably withhold consent to a Vendor assignment.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Client’s approval of an assignment by TrueLink shall not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that TrueLink shall not assign to a competitor of Client.

elements.element: Customer’s change of control must not give Vendor a right to terminate the Agreement.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that a change of control of Client shall not give TrueLink any right to terminate the Agreement.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Client may assign without approval to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, covering the stated customary successor transactions.

elements.element: Customer must provide written notice when assigning to a successor.
elements.evidence: No written-notice obligation applies to Client’s successor assignment.

elements.element: Vendor may assign to a successor without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: There is no successor-assignment exception for TrueLink; absent the affiliate exception, prior written Client approval remains required.

elements.element: Vendor must provide written notice when assigning to a successor.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no written-notice mechanism for a TrueLink successor assignment.

elements.element: Every Customer assignment other than an assignment to a successor requires Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Client may assign to a financially responsible affiliate without TrueLink approval, even though such an assignment need not be a successor assignment.

elements.element: Vendor must not unreasonably withhold consent to a Customer assignment other than an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The clause does not state that TrueLink’s approval of a Client assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Every Vendor assignment other than an assignment to a successor requires Customer consent.
elements.evidence: TrueLink may assign to a financially responsible affiliate without Client approval, and assignments to Client competitors are prohibited rather than permitted subject to consent.

elements.element: Customer must not unreasonably withhold consent to a Vendor assignment other than an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The clause states generally that Client’s approval of an assignment by TrueLink shall not be unreasonably withheld.

result.reason: The redline does not reach either complete position. It retains a consent-free Vendor affiliate-assignment right, contrary to the preferred one-way Vendor consent requirement, and limits Customer’s affiliate right to financially responsible affiliates. It also lacks the fallback’s mutual successor right and written-notice duties, and does not impose a reasonableness standard on Vendor’s consent to Customer assignments. The operative additions are otherwise generally coherent and do not disturb unrelated commercial terms.
